segment.description: Duck River mainstem from Columbia (Maury County) down through the Western Highland Rim to its confluence with the Tennessee River (Kentucky Reservoir) near New Johnsonville (Humphreys County), roughly 100 river miles through Maury, Hickman and Humphreys counties. TWRA documents it as a warmwater catfish/bass float river; no trout program exists on this reach.
segment.boundaries: Columbia (Riverwalk Park, the most downstream impoundment on the Duck per TWRA) to the Tennessee River confluence near New Johnsonville. Bracketed by USGS 03601990 'Duck River at Hwy 100 at Centerville' (Hickman Co., 35.7842/-87.4600, HUC 06040003) and USGS 03603000 'Duck River above Hurricane Mills' (Humphreys Co., 35.9301/-87.7431, HUC 06040003).

damTailwater.note: No dam tailwater on this reach: TWRA calls Riverwalk Park in Columbia 'the most downstream impoundment on the Duck River'. The nearest trout-relevant release (Normandy Dam tailwater) ends at Three Forks Bridge far upstream above Shelbyville - a different catalog reach entirely.

coldSource.notes: TWRA describes Centerville-to-mouth habitat as 'large pools, snags and trees, sand bars, and long wide shoals' - lowland warmwater structure. TDEC's scenic-river page documents the river's confluence with the Tennessee River near New Johnsonville; the receiving water is Kentucky Reservoir, a warmwater mainstem reservoir. No cold-water mechanism is documented anywhere consulted.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation exists and no trout are stocked on this reach: the TWRA stocking workbook has zero Duck-mainstem rows in Maury/Hickman/Humphreys. Seasonal rainbow programs in the same counties (Cane Creek and Mill Creek, Hickman Co.; Hurricane Creek, Humphreys Co.) are separate small creeks, not the Duck mainstem. TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027: hatchery-supported streams are 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented on the lower Duck. TWRA's page describes the reach's fishery as catfish (Columbia-Centerville 'among the best for catfish in middle Tennessee') and warmwater habitat; rock bass are noted as more abundant upstream of Columbia.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Reach-specific USGS/TDEC grab records show summer water of 29 deg C at Centerville and up to 33.5 deg C above Hurricane Mills, and TWRA documents the reach purely as a warmwater catfish/bass river with no trout stocking anywhere from Columbia to the mouth.
